rationale: Accordion keeps secondary information available without making every section visible at once.
The ZIP reference defines card surface, 56px triggers, meta text, chevron spring, and height animation.
Use it for detail inside profiles, drawers, settings, and help content; not for primary navigation.

items.rule: Groups related disclosure rows in one card-like surface.
Button row with title, optional icon, optional meta, and expanded state.
Shows disclosure direction and rotates with spring motion.
Animates height and keeps collapsed content out of tab order.
Separate rows without turning each row into a separate card.

items: Connect trigger and content when implementation exposes IDs.
Collapsed content must not receive keyboard focus.
Enter and Space toggle the active trigger.
Do not hide critical required content by default.

variants.copy: Accordion variants describe disclosure behavior: single, multiple, metadata, icon-led, and compact.

demos.label: Single open
demos.description: Only one section is open at a time.

demos.label: Compact
demos.description: Dense setting rows with short content.

states.copy: Accordion states describe availability, disclosure, focus, disabled behavior, and closed rows.

demos.label: Focus row
demos.description: Keyboard focus is visible on the trigger.

demos.label: Multiple row
demos.description: More than one section can stay open.

variant-state-behavior.copy: Variant sets disclosure model; state controls whether each row is open, closed, focused, disabled, or default.

full-width.copy: Accordion may fill its container, but each row keeps stable trigger height and content rhythm.

responsive-layout-patterns.copy: Accordion stacks naturally on all viewports. On phones, keep titles short and avoid hiding required actions.

viewport-organization.copy: Use Accordion where detail belongs to the same object. Use Tabs for parallel views and Drawer for larger workspace expansion.

items.title: Phone

items.title: Tablet
items.rule: Use metadata to summarize hidden detail.

items.title: Desktop
items.rule: Use for secondary detail in panels and profiles.

Raw visual or motion values are used.

miel.copy: MIEL treats Accordion as secondary disclosure: agents can use it to organize related detail, but humans confirm whether hidden content is safe to collapse.
canDecide: Use for secondary detail inside the same object.
Use metadata when collapsed rows need summary.
mustAsk: The hidden content is required to complete the task.
Multiple open sections may create long, hard-to-scan pages.
rejectIf: Keyboard and aria-expanded behavior is undefined.
miel.handoff: I am using Accordion for secondary detail. Please confirm which content can be collapsed, default open row, metadata, and whether multiple rows may stay open.
